heading: INT. ABANDONED DRIVE-IN - PROJECTION TOWER - DUSK

units.text: INT. ABANDONED DRIVE-IN - PROJECTION TOWER - DUSK
A concrete tower at the back of a cracked lot, its screen peeling to bare plywood.
Weeds climb through the speaker posts.
Dusk throws long orange bars through the broken shutters, and the air smells of old popcorn oil and rust.
Four kids crowd the single room.
A battered projector squats on a table, its lens clouded.
Reels of film stand stacked like cheese wheels.
A folding chair, a cooler, a radio playing low.
CASSIUS "CASS" MWANGI, 17, lanky, a hand-me-down varsity jacket two sizes too small, sits cross-legged on the cooler, picking at a loose thread.
He is the one who found the place and he knows it.
FLORENCIA "FLO" RUIZ-ABERNATHY, 16, braids tied up in a bandanna, perches on the table's edge swinging her boots.
She watches Cass the way one watches a campfire that might spread.
HENRIK SOLBERG, 17, glasses taped at the hinge, kneels over the projector with a screwdriver, fully absorbed.
He hasn't spoken in ten minutes.
And in the corner, half in shadow, PILAR TRAN, 15, hugs her knees and says nothing, a camera hanging from her neck.
You said it'd work.
units.name: FLO

units.text: I said it might.
units.name: CASS

units.text: You said it would.
units.name: FLO

units.text: It might work. It's a hundred years old.
units.name: CASS

units.text: It's from 1974.
units.name: HENRIK

units.text: Same thing.
units.name: CASS

units.text: It is emphatically not the same thing.
units.name: HENRIK

units.text: Pilar lifts her camera.
Clicks.
The shutter is loud in the small room.
Cass flinches.
Don't.
units.name: CASS

units.text: It's good light.
units.name: PILAR

units.text: I look stupid.
units.name: CASS

units.text: You look like yourself.
units.name: PILAR

units.text: That's what I mean.
units.name: CASS

units.text: Flo snorts.
Henrik snaps a panel shut and rises, wiping his hands.
Try it.
units.name: HENRIK

units.text: Cass slides off the cooler.
Crosses to the projector.
His hand hovers over the switch.
What if it's just a blank screen?
units.name: CASS

units.text: Then we've wasted a Friday.
units.name: FLO

units.text: We've wasted a lot of Fridays.
units.name: CASS

units.text: So one more won't matter.
units.name: FLO

units.text: A beat.
He throws the switch.
The projector shudders, coughs, and a rectangle of white fire leaps from the lens across the lot, striking the peeling screen.
Nothing.
Just white.
Then a flicker.
A number counts down: 5, 4, 3.
They hold their breath.
Henrik, Flo, Pilar, all drawn to the beam.
It's working.
units.name: HENRIK

units.text: The reel catches.
The screen shows a black-and-white shot of a woman on a porch, lit from behind, smiling at someone off camera.
She holds the smile a long time.
Then she turns and looks directly into the lens.
Who is that?
units.name: PILAR

units.text: It was on the shelf. It had your name on it.
units.name: CASS

units.text: It did not.
units.name: PILAR

units.text: It said TRAN.
units.name: CASS

units.text: There are a lot of Trans.
units.name: PILAR

units.text: In Barlow? There's one.
units.name: CASS

units.text: Pilar stands.
Her camera swings from its strap.
On the screen the woman mouths something, long and slow.
Pilar steps closer to the beam, enormous shadows flung across the lot.
Pilar?
units.name: FLO

units.text: She's my grandmother.
units.name: PILAR

units.text: You said your grandmother lived in Hanoi.
units.name: HENRIK

units.text: She did.
units.name: PILAR

units.text: So how did she end up on a porch in Ohio in 1974?
units.name: HENRIK

units.text: I don't know.
units.name: PILAR

units.text: I thought it'd be nice. A surprise.
units.name: CASS

units.text: You thought.
units.name: PILAR

units.text: I thought--
units.name: CASS

units.text: You didn't ask me.
units.name: PILAR

units.text: It was supposed to be a gift.
units.name: CASS

units.text: It's my family, Cass! It's mine!
units.name: PILAR

units.text: Her voice cracks off the concrete.
The film keeps rolling: the woman on the porch, laughing now, silent and radiant.
Flo moves to Pilar's side but doesn't touch her.
Henrik switches off the radio.
In the stillness the projector chatters.
Let her watch.
units.name: FLO

units.text: Cass backs away until his shoulders hit the wall.
He stares at the floor.
Pilar stands in the light, shadow thrown huge across the screen, the grandmother's face drifting across her own.
She raises the camera.
Takes a single photograph of the screen.
Then she lowers it and sits down on the floor, and the others, without a word, settle around her.
